item.title: Re: In the blink of an eye
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via pm
Hello! Interesting SCP you've got there!
It would be a shame if someone…
Critiqued it…

+ show block
– hide block

Imma be honest..I kinda like this idea!
The only thing is I'm not sure if the Foundation would be the one too something like this. Combining humans with anomalous items seems something more like a Sarkic thing to do. Maybe the Agent gets left behind/capture during a raid on a Sarkic base, resulting in a ritual/experiment on her being performed that gives her those eyes? You can choose to keep/reject its idea, but just make sure it remains belivable.
My other concern is that the agent might become a bit omnipotent, so I think you should give some sort of consequence to her power and/or make them less strong. Maybe she starts to go insane or looses her free will/higher brain function, reducing her to little more than a mindless robot used by the foundation to do their dirty work.
I'm really close to greenlighting this. If you can just fix those two concerns, I'm more than willing to give you the go ahead. Best of luck, and please PM me if you want me to take another look!

item.title: Re: House of Memories
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via pm
That's an interesting SCP you've got there!
It would be a shame if someone…
Critiqued it…

+ show block
– hide block

I'll be honest and upfront about this idea: it seems really wishy-washy, and as Plague said in his reply, you're not going in a singe concise direction. You need to reign in you story, and focus on one particular aspect of it. Aside from that, there are some plot points that really do irk me. HEre are a few concerns I have:

  • Origin: So, a kid's grandmother just happens to know a spell that can curse households? It seems really out of the blue, and it doesn't really seem like you thought your concept through. I get each scp doesn't need to have a clear origin or discovery story, but what you have just seems too random for my liking.
  • Cliche: It's clear your trying to evoke some emotional response in your audience, specifically fear, but the way you're describing it right now just doesn't fit. There's a lot of SCPs on this site that deal with past traumas/memories. While no concept is 100% unique and original, yours does rely too much on pre-existing tropes
  • Believability: I highly doubt that the Foundation would Raise kids for the sole purpose of making them into D-Class. That's not how the Foundation works. More than likely, the kids would be amnesticized and released into society, killed if they are too dangerous to be kept around (which I doubt would happen), or classified as SCPs themselves.

You really need to tighten up your story. It's fine if you take a couple days to reply or edit your response: you just need to ensure that it's something appealing to your audience, including your critiquers. As of right now, no greenlight, but if you want me to come take another look, do PM me!
Best of luck

item.title: Re: Television POV(Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Summoned by PM

The premise here is an interesting one depending on what you do with it. It would be very easy to turn this into a "thing that does a thing" with nothing else - essentially that's what the anomaly is - but if you do something interesting narratively and really explore the effects of this anomaly properly, I think this could be an interesting premise for an article.

Exploring a series of unique vignettes could work, but you'd need to find a way to build them towards a conclusive end that leaves the reader feeling satisfied, and that won't be super easy to do. I'd recommend trying to build a more traditional narrative for your first article. Give us a clear series of events that you're going to tell - that's the core of any good SCP article, a clear narrative. If you've got that, you're on a strong start. The anomaly doesn't necessarily lend itself to a traditional narrative without a bit of work, but you've started that process by having it create an effect in people who watch their own perspective. Try to expand on that in terms of what stories you might tell with it, perhaps. Maybe it causes some serious problems that the Foundation then has to solve, or perhaps it's an addictive feeling, or maybe the Foundation thinks they can use the SCP to try and control people and anomalies in some way.

Whatever you go with, the core thing this needs is a clearer central narrative, with a beginning, middle, and end. What's the story you're going to tell here, in detail? That's the key.

item.title: Re: Can someone explain the entirety of the Scarlet King lore?
item.content:encoded:
Check the scarlet-king tag. Note, however, that the lack of canon applies much more to Big Red than to standardized, fleshed-out things like Sarkicism and the CotBG, so you’re going to run into some contradictions.

One of the most compelling elements of the Scarlet King mythos is the mystery. Unlike most other anomalous religions, most of the cultists are wiped out and the Foundation is left trying to piece things together from the artifacts they left behind. Toss in the subterfuge going on with 2317 and 231’s implications that the Foundation’s been infiltrated or something, and you have a situation where the people in-universe are probably just as confused about it as the reader.

item.title: Re: Blood Bowl Hell (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Quoting Silence of the Lambs as a "socially responsible" movie is especially concerning, considering it was widely panned by LGBT audiences for its incredibly irresponsible depiction of transsexuality (no matter how much it tried to backtrack with its Blanchardist "fake trans" pseudoscientific nonsense).

An important thing to keep in mind when you're handling sensitive topics: what are you actually trying to say? A charitable take on the piece for me is that it's trying to make a point about how misogyny is ingrained into the Japanese traditionalist zeitgeist; however, it doesn't feel like there's any attempt to analyze how that's the case. Instead, it feels like a titillating backdrop to an action-horror piece, or at least that's what I got from the Central Narrative.

This is vitally important for any piece handling sensitive topics, because the alternative is letting your piece degenerate into an "exploitation piece", e.g. something that depicts the topics with an almost voyeuristic aloofness and no real attempt to make a point on it, which severely limits the audience your piece can engage with.

Forum thread: Blood Bowl Hell (Seeking Greenlight)

item.title: Re: What award would somebody get for neutralizing a keter?
item.content:encoded:
Nothing. If this dude can neutralize 106 or some other impossible to destroy, nearly impossible to contain anomaly he could also flatten site 19 or eradicate the O5 council from existence, or make himself the supreme God emperor of earth or something. Reality benders are too powerful and too unpredictable for a control-freak organization like the Foundation to tolerate, no matter how cooperative they are, because they might become uncooperative in the future. That’s why most of the free-willed reality benders with full control of their powers in the SCP verse have either been decommissioned by Clef or liquidated by the GOC. If your character destroyed 106, the foundation would send Dr. Clef to kill him or otherwise make sure he doesn’t get the chance to destroy anything else.

Also, don’t make a superhero character and beat up 682. That’s a Mary Sue and the Worf Effect. Anomalous people, regardless of how helpful they ostensibly are, are monsters at worse and the victims of a terrible condition at best. If it has powers that you would like to have, it’s not an SCP. As a general rule, anyway.

item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Explorers
item.content:encoded:
Hello,

my pen name is Galvaude and I'm really looking into participating in this awesome community. I discovered the SCP Foundation through the "Infographic Show" short's. The video of SCP-1981 really made me want to dig more into the SCP universe and here I am!

I've always liked horror-ish stories with mind-breaking technology and moral twisting entities ; from Poe to Warhammer 40k. I am here to contribute to the SPC universe with, I hope, interesting content for the readers/community to enjoy. I have studied political science, more specificaly political philosohpy, and I believe this will show in my future SPC stories. I also really enjoy discussing ideas and concepts, so I'm willing to engage in any on-going discussions! English is not my first langage, although I had to learn it at a young age. My first langage is french (Canada).

As for my hobbies, I DM, I play videogames (mostly RPGs - Big fan of the Baldur's Gate saga), and write poetry, short stories, make experimental videos, etc… my hobbies are always artistic but with a situationnist touch (check out what is situationnism). This is one of the reason I joined this community ; I feel like the collective approach is definitly situationnist in it's nature (being collective and anonymous). I like it alot!

As for the SCP, I am definitly intrigued (more and more) about the Thaumiel class. I have read all the SCPs that are listed under this class and I am fascinated by the boundary between the Keter and Thaumiel class (like SCP-1968). I think I'm going to dig deeper into that relation and on how the foundation deals with that. If anyone would be kind enough to guide me through existing conflictual/boundary-crossing SPCs and potential debates on classes, that would be really nice :). Of course, this is not to proove that the S/E/K/T(N) system does not work, it is just that I like to swim in uncharted waters.

I am definitly looking into making SCP articles, and I really appreciate the peer-reviewed system that is established here.

As per the december question, I think my answer relates to the colours you see when you close your eyes. I always wonder if I can control them or not, and if I could control them, would the patterns be as pretty? And then I fall asleep lol

Cheers and Merry Christmas lol
-Galvaude

item.title: Re: Looking for Greenlights | The Stardust Solution
item.content:encoded:
If this blackhole was made by someone trying to restart the universe, why did they put a time delay on it? Theoretically, if the creator has the ability to dictate how the new universe would form, surely they have the ability to just restart it immediately.

I'm just not getting a cohesive feel from this. You seem real intent on using the "actually this has happened before" hook and the change in Stonewood's character as the main thrust but these have been seen in other SCPs many times over — I'm not certain it'll really stick with readers.

Have you considered if the singularity angle is really the best way to go about telling this story? As a ball of energy it doesn't have much character on its own, and this creator person who we should be connected to isn't really in play. I've seen Doomsday SCPs about toilet paper, satellites, and cheap computer games, and they generally tend to stick with people more.

item.title: SCP Idea - Security Blanket
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: No

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama

Page Layout (Optional): Interview Logs, Incident Reports

Elevator Pitch: A young orphan boy is found in possession of a quilt with anomalous properties. He is also being stalked by anomalous entities who wish to take the blanket from him.

Central Narrative: An MTF team is sent to a small farmhouse where anomalous events have been reported. During their sweep the team a young boy appears out of nowhere, clutching a quilt with strange designs. The MTF team convince the boy to accompany them back to a site, where the boy is interviewed by SCP personnel.

The boy reveals that his grandmother, who recently died, gave him the quilt, explaining that it would protect him. Study of the quilt reveals that the designs on it are thaumaturgical symbols of protection, and while in the boy's possession, it displays a number of functions. When he hides under it, the boy cannot be perceived. When wrapped around him, the quilt protects him from physical harm. It can also slowly heal wounds. When he ties it around his neck like a cape, it allows the boy to fly. What's more, while the boy can willingly surrender the quilt, if it's forcibly taken, it returns to him in a matter of moments.

+ show block
– hide block

During his detainment, the boy also explains that the quilt protects him from "the bad things." These "bad things" are anomalous entities that manage to penetrate the site and seem to exhibit ghost-like abilities. SCP personnel discover that they're drawn to the blanket rather than the boy, as the child exhibits no anomalous qualities. The "bad things" also appear blind to the quilt when it's inert, so it's simply a matter of encouraging the child to surrender the quilt. However, SCP personnel find it difficult to convince him to give up the last thing connecting him to his family.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Aside from the fact that the quilt's anomalous properties are as limitless as the boy's imagination, the central drama of a boy getting over the loss of his family and learning to accept what happened and move on would make for a good narrative. While applying amnestics would normally solve the problem, in this case the quilt allows him to resist the amnestics, as he doesn't want to forget. Surrendering the quilt will make him safe, but it'll also be giving up a part of himself.

Additional Notes: Any assistance with formulating the anomalous "bad things" would be greatly appreciated, as that's not fully fleshed-out yet.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

item.title: Re: Scp 5133
item.content:encoded:
+Let's do it!
-Let's do it!

I won't mince words here; this entire concept page is quite messy and doesn't fully convey everything I need to know about your idea.

5133 gets contained for an anomaly that has is blocked by personnel

I have no idea what you're trying to say here.

as any description of appearance or behavior will cause the people involved to worship Scp 5133.

Just like any number of mind-altering, compulsion anomalies. Uninteresting.

Well, even bland anomalies can be passable if the story execution is good enough, so let's take a look at that.

two mtf operatives go to try to contain any escaped anomaly's after believing that site 138 had suffered a containment breach.

A false containment breach could be a good Hook if this idea wasn't so messy as well as just plain incomplete. What is the anomaly? All we get is that it's probably Memetic, and that it gives you a compulsion to worship it.

Perfect containment cant be made as the original anomoly can be discovered and cared for if no information can be learnt.

I'm going to assume 'can be discovered and cared for if no information can be learnt' was intentional. So, the best way to contain it is to…not know about it?

By that logic, just destroying all data files on it and administering amnestics would be the way to go.

I'm sorry, but I'm immensely not feeling this.

'Non-descript thing you can't know about' has the potential to be interesting, especially with a false containment breach, but this is severely underdeveloped and was so messily presented, picking through it was more difficult than it should have been.

My immediate recommendation would be to find a way to make the Anomaly less bland. Develop that.

Second, make this page kess messy.

Apologies if this was harsh.

Anywho, I hope I helped and I bid you a good day. 👍

P.S. I recommend not choosing an SCP number while you're still trying to obtain Greenlights. SCPs in development are labelled as SCP-XXXX. The SCP-5133 slot could be taken well before you get to it. It's a possibility.

item.title: Phantom limb syndrome but with a twist [Greenlight]
item.content:encoded:
Patients have never been amputated nor were they born with any missing limbs. However, they can still feel…something. Something that should not be there.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout: starting out with an old version of the SCP article, along with obvious clarification that is it outdated and a new one is currently under review. Interviews that lead up to the revelation. Researchers notes / thoughts

Elevator Pitch: The premise is that this SCP is essentially a version of the Phantom limb syndrome…at least that’s what it appears to be. The difference is that it affects people who have all their limbs. Those affected people feel limbs that normally do not exist on humans, such as a third arm or leg. Some may even feel multiple ones.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: It caught the attention of some researchers, it wasn't exactly deemed a threat, since patients behaved normally, besides the weird sensations that come with feeling extra limbs.
After some more discoveries were made, the research team realized that there is a bit more to it. Not exactly dangerous, just…strange. It is more than just a sensation. Eventually, this would lead them to the realization that the SCP is not simply phantom limb syndrome but actually a sort of bridge between multiple realities. Patients are connected to lifeforms from another reality that possess the limbs they feel.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: It is a very passive SCP. Not an alternate dimensions, not a crazy creature, not a disease, etc. The SCP itself is a bridge between dimensions, at least two. This opens up a lot of storytelling opportunities relating to other dimensions but more in the sense of how the dimensions interact.

Additional Notes: I'm still debating how deep I should delve into this other reality but right now, I find it more interesting if it is seen as something that the Foundation needs to explore once they find out how to actually access this reality. I’d appreciate feedback about the general idea and that kind of multiple dimension connection.

Looking forward to some feedback. Happy holidays! :)

item.title: Re: Blood Bowl Hell (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Thank you very much for your response; it's honestly really appreciated.

I understand your qualms. I personally believe that a story can portray cruelty in a socially responsible manner, as long as it unambiguously establishes that such cruelty is wrong, ala Silence of the Lambs. I also would have to make sure that these characters are not empty vessels existing only for suffering, but fleshed out characters who just so happen to also suffer. Just out of curiosity, in what place(s) do I cross the line in your eyes, so I can avoid doing so in the future?

Also, regarding the Shinto vs Buddhism thing: the reason I wanted it to be a Shinto priest was actually because they aren't Buddhist. I wanted it to come off as a "the Buddhists say this, but it's not my religion and it all seems kinda freaky to me" kinda thing. I completely understand though that it came off like I didn't know what I was talking about. Are there any other instances in there that seem to indicate a lack of understanding on my part?

Again, thank you very much for responding. While you clearly don't like my idea, I appreciate you taking the time out of your day to read it and explain your qualms. Merry Christmas!
